## Purpose

This report compares the dataset produced by `Codex_Script.R`
(`Codex_Script_MergedData.csv`) with the original dataset
(`Merged_Data.csv`). Both files are read directly from `data/processed`, so
the tables update automatically if either file is regenerated.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(purrr)
library(knitr)

processed_dir <- if (dir.exists("data/processed")) "data/processed" else "../data/processed"
codex <- read_csv(file.path(processed_dir, "Codex_Script_MergedData.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
original <- read_csv(file.path(processed_dir, "Merged_Data.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

dataset_summary <- function(data, dataset) {
  tibble(
    dataset = dataset, rows = nrow(data), columns = ncol(data),
    countries = n_distinct(data$iso),
    first_year = min(data$year, na.rm = TRUE), last_year = max(data$year, na.rm = TRUE),
    unique_country_years = nrow(distinct(data, iso, year)),
    duplicated_country_year_rows = sum(duplicated(data[c("iso", "year")]))
  )
}
```

## Dataset structure

```{r}
bind_rows(
  dataset_summary(codex, "Codex script"),
  dataset_summary(original, "Original script")
) |>
  kable(caption = "Structural comparison of the two output files")
```

Both outputs now have one row per country-year. The corrected original file
has the same 2000--2019 analysis frame as the Codex output, with no duplicated
country-year keys.

```{r}
all_columns <- union(names(codex), names(original))
tibble(
  variable = all_columns,
  in_codex_output = all_columns %in% names(codex),
  in_original_output = all_columns %in% names(original)
) |>
  kable(caption = "Variables included in each output file")
```

The Codex output uses consistent lower-case mortality names and adds
`armed_conflict`. The original output instead retains `total_conflicts` and
`binary_conflict`; its mortality variable names retain capital letters. Both
outputs include the earthquake and drought indicators and all eight covariates:
`gdp_1000`,
`oecd`, `pop_dens`, `urban`, `age_dep`, `male_edu`, `temp`, and
`rainfall_1000`.

## Country-year coverage

```{r}
codex_keys <- codex |> distinct(iso, year)
original_keys <- original |> distinct(iso, year)

tibble(
  comparison = c("Country-years in both files", "Only in Codex output", "Only in original output"),
  n_country_years = c(
    nrow(inner_join(codex_keys, original_keys, by = c("iso", "year"))),
    nrow(anti_join(codex_keys, original_keys, by = c("iso", "year"))),
    nrow(anti_join(original_keys, codex_keys, by = c("iso", "year")))
  )
) |>
  kable(caption = "Overlap in country-year keys")
```

The two files have identical country-year coverage after the disaster merge
was corrected. Therefore, each comparison in the next section is a direct
one-to-one comparison of the same country-year records.

## Agreement in comparable variables

The corrected original file already has one row per country-year. Its mortality
variable names are harmonised below solely to permit a direct comparison with
the Codex output; neither source dataset is altered.

```{r}
original_harmonised <- original |>
  rename(
    neonatal_mortality = Neonatal_Mortality,
    infant_mortality = Infant_Mortality,
    under5_mortality = Under5_Mortality
  )

comparable_variables <- c(
  "maternal_mortality", "neonatal_mortality", "infant_mortality",
  "under5_mortality", "earthquake", "drought", "gdp_1000", "oecd",
  "pop_dens", "urban", "age_dep", "male_edu", "temp", "rainfall_1000"
)

comparison_data <- codex |>
  select(iso, year, all_of(comparable_variables)) |>
  inner_join(
    original_harmonised |> select(iso, year, all_of(comparable_variables)),
    by = c("iso", "year"), suffix = c("_codex", "_original")
  )

agreement <- map_dfr(comparable_variables, function(variable) {
  codex_value <- comparison_data[[paste0(variable, "_codex")]]
  original_value <- comparison_data[[paste0(variable, "_original")]]
  tibble(
    variable = variable,
    matched_non_missing = sum(!is.na(codex_value) & !is.na(original_value)),
    equal_values = sum(!is.na(codex_value) & !is.na(original_value) & abs(codex_value - original_value) < 1e-10),
    differing_values = sum(!is.na(codex_value) & !is.na(original_value) & abs(codex_value - original_value) >= 1e-10),
    missing_only_in_codex = sum(is.na(codex_value) & !is.na(original_value)),
    missing_only_in_original = sum(!is.na(codex_value) & is.na(original_value))
  )
})
```

```{r}
agreement |>
  kable(caption = "Value agreement across matched country-year records")
```

The mortality measures and covariates agree wherever both files have a value,
because they originate from the same raw CSV files. The apparent differences
in `earthquake` and `drought` are a missingness convention: the Codex file
codes a country-year with no disaster record as `0`, whereas the original file
codes it as `NA`. The disaster-event rows (`1`) agree. This convention matters
for modelling because `NA` values may cause observations to be excluded,
whereas `0` explicitly represents no recorded event.

## Conflict variables

The corrected original file now includes an `armed_conflict` indicator, so it
can be compared directly with the Codex indicator.

```{r}
conflict_comparison <- codex |>
  select(iso, year, armed_conflict_codex = armed_conflict) |>
  inner_join(
    original |> select(iso, year, armed_conflict_original = armed_conflict),
    by = c("iso", "year")
  ) |>
  mutate(matches = armed_conflict_codex == armed_conflict_original)

tibble(
  country_years_compared = nrow(conflict_comparison),
  matching_indicators = sum(conflict_comparison$matches),
  differing_indicators = sum(!conflict_comparison$matches)
) |>
  kable(caption = "Agreement in the armed-conflict indicator")
```

```{r}
conflict_comparison |>
  filter(!matches) |>
  arrange(iso, year) |>
  kable(caption = "Country-years with different armed-conflict values")
```

The remaining disagreements are limited to 13 country-years. They likely
reflect the point at which the 25-death threshold is applied: the Codex script
applies it to each conflict-country-year before combining conflicts, whereas
the original calculation may apply it after summing conflicts within a
country-year.

## Conclusion

Both outputs are now analysis-ready at the country-year level: they have the
same coverage, unique country-year keys, matching mortality and covariate
values, and the requested covariates. The only substantive differences are the
disaster missingness convention (`0` in Codex versus `NA` in the original) and
the armed-conflict indicator in 13 country-years. Column-name differences and
the representation of missing values are otherwise formatting differences.
